title: Contrast tip mittens
subtitle: Full mittens in DK with a contrast colour finger tip.
excerpt: Full mittens in DK wool, worked in the round in stocking stitch, with a contrast colour added at the finger tip. A simple way to introduce two yarns without any colourwork chart. Afterthought thumb. Sized for hand circumferences of 18, 20, and 22 cm.
sourceNotes: Contrast-tip mittens synthesised from the standard DK mitten construction, with a single colour-join at the tip. The colour-join technique follows standard knitting practice.

glossaryTerms.definition: A thumb opening made by working the thumb stitches in waste yarn during the hand, then returning after the hand is complete. The waste yarn is removed to reveal live stitches which are picked up and worked as the thumb.
A method for knitting small circumferences in the round on one long circular needle. The cable is pulled into a loop at the midpoint so each half of the stitches sits on its own needle tip.

content.text: Full mittens in DK wool, worked in stocking stitch in the round, with a contrast colour at the finger tip and an
afterthought thumb
. Sized for hand circumferences of 18, 20, and 22 cm.

The contrast tip is the simplest way to introduce a second colour to a mitten. There is no chart and no stranding; one yarn is simply tied off and the other begins at a clean round join. The result is a bold stripe at the tip of the mitten. The construction uses
magic loop
on a long circular. Budget about 85 g of MC (185 m / 200 yards) and 15 g of CC (33 m / 36 yards), both DK.
What you need

items.name: MC (main colour)
items.qty: 85 g (about 185 m / 200 yards) of DK-weight wool

items.name: CC (contrast colour)
items.qty: 15 g (about 33 m / 36 yards) of the same yarn in a contrasting colour

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 3.75 mm (UK 9 / US 5) circular needle, at least 80 cm cable, for magic loop

items.name: Stitch markers
items.qty: 3: 1 for beginning of round, 1 for thumb, 1 for midpoint at top shaping

items.name: Waste yarn
items.qty: About 30 cm of smooth contrasting yarn for the afterthought thumb

content.text: Gauge
22 stitches and 28 rounds to 10 cm in stocking stitch on 3.75 mm needles. Swatch in MC before casting on.
Pattern
Before you cast on, circle your size. Every stitch count reads S (M, L) for hand circumferences 18 (20, 22) cm.
Cast on and cuff
Using MC and the long-tail cast-on, cast on 40 (44, 48) stitches. Join to work in the round. Work 24 (26, 28) rounds of 2x2 rib.
Hand body

Switch to stocking stitch in MC. Work 10 (12, 12) rounds. Place the thumb: work the first 10 (11, 12) stitches with waste yarn, slip back, and work those stitches again in MC. Continue in MC stocking stitch for 20 (22, 24) more rounds.
Contrast tip
Cut MC. Join CC at the beginning of the round. Work 4 rounds in CC stocking stitch.
Top shaping

Place a marker at the midpoint (between stitches 20/21, 22/23, or 24/25). Decrease round in CC: k1, ssk, knit to 3 before midpoint, k2tog, k1, SM, k1, ssk, knit to last 3, k2tog, k1. Plain round. Repeat until 8 stitches remain. Draw CC through and close.
Thumb
Remove waste yarn and pick up 10 (11, 12) stitches above and 10 (11, 12) below the gap. Work 14 (16, 16) rounds in MC stocking stitch. Bind off.
Common faults
Loose stitch at the colour join: the first stitch in CC was worked with a loose tail. When joining the new colour, hold both tails snug for the first 2 or 3 stitches.
Colour join line is not straight: the end-of-round marker shifted during the last MC round. Re-check the marker position before cutting MC.
Finishing
Weave in both tails at the colour join on the wrong side, one going each direction along the join row.
Care
Hand wash in cool water. Lay flat to dry. If the two colours bleed, wash separately until the water runs clear.
What to try next
Add a second contrast at the cuff as well, to echo the tip colour. Or try child striped mittens to explore carrying two yarns in a more structured stripe sequence.
